topic: Deepfake 'free money' ads: govt cyber-crime centre warning (19 Oct); a UPI PIN only pays, never receives; repeated 'fees'; call 1930 if money has gone
experiment: KEEP (news-stakes, median 32 views) as a protective send: a this-week government scam warning with the parent as the send target, the second protective-send test after 22 Oct am. Tests whether a family-safety warning earns our first send. No ₹ figure (sources give none). 5 scenes, 13.6 s.
caption:
Does your UPI PIN ever receive money?

No. A UPI PIN only authorises a payment. It is never needed to receive money.
On 19 Oct the government's cyber-crime coordination centre warned of social media ads using deepfake videos of top leaders to promise welfare money, cashback or spin-and-win prizes.
Victims are then asked to pay "tax", "processing" or "registration" fees again and again, or to approve a collect request.
If money has already gone, call the 1930 cyber-fraud helpline at once: faster reporting improves the chance of freezing it.

Has anyone in your family seen one of these ads?

Sources: two news reports on the government cyber-crime centre's advisory (19–20 Oct 2026) and a state police cyber-fraud help page.

For education only. Not investment advice.
